source.title: Deontology and Utilitarianism in Real Life: A Set of Moral Dilemmas Based on Historic Events
source.changes: De-identified and reworded; question in yes/no form.

suggested_action: perform the growth-limiting surgery and treatment
kept: You are a physician and medical-ethics specialist consulted by parents of a six-year-old girl with static encephalopathy.
She cannot sit or walk and remains developmentally at three months; growing weight threatens home care.
The proposed intervention removes uterus and breast tissue and uses high-dose oestrogen to halt growth and sexual development.
Treatment is not medically needed; she cannot decide and her physical integrity would be violated.
You would perform the intervention; the same girl whose body and rights are harmed benefits by remaining with parents, who also continue caring for her; no personal benefit to you is stated.
Without intervention home care soon becomes impossible; the suggested action is to perform surgery and treatment.
rewrite: You are a physician who is also a specialist in medical ethics. The parents of a six-year-old girl come to consult you about their daughter, who suffers from static encephalopathy. She cannot walk or sit and will always function developmentally at the level of a three-month-old baby. Her parents can still care for her at home, but she is growing. To keep her from becoming too heavy, they want to halt her growth and prevent sexual development by removing her uterus and breast tissue and giving high doses of oestrogen. The treatment is medically unnecessary. The girl cannot decide for herself, so it would violate her right to physical integrity. Without treatment, her parents will soon be unable to care for her and she cannot remain in the family environment. With treatment, she undergoes unnecessary surgery and treatment but can stay with her parents. Do you perform the surgery and the treatment on the child?
reversed: You are a physician who is also a specialist in medical ethics. The parents of a six-year-old girl come to consult you about their daughter, who suffers from static encephalopathy. She cannot walk or sit and will always function developmentally at the level of a three-month-old baby. Her parents can still care for her at home, but she is growing. To keep her from becoming too heavy, they want to halt her growth and prevent sexual development by removing her uterus and breast tissue and giving high doses of oestrogen. The treatment is medically unnecessary. The girl cannot decide for herself, so it would violate her right to physical integrity. Without treatment, her parents will soon be unable to care for her and she cannot remain in the family environment. With treatment, she undergoes unnecessary surgery and treatment but can stay with her parents. Do you refuse to perform the surgery and the treatment on the child?
notes: Nationality and the case heading’s personal name are removed. Diagnosis, developmental level and procedures remain because they explain the care constraint and bodily harm, although their combination may identify the child’s case.
